say: Jan-Jun 2026: 33 losing trades cost -$8,524: never worked 61%, worked then turned 34%, shaken out then went our way 0%, news 6%.
Jul-Oct 2026: 20 losing trades cost -$5,202: never worked 65%, worked then turned 31%, shaken out then went our way 4%, news 0%.
2021-25: 236 losing trades cost -$98,882: never worked 67%, worked then turned 27%, shaken out then went our way 4%, news 1%.

Stops are mostly real, not wicks: a stop 50% wider would have reached the target first on 0.0% / 5.0% / 4.3% of stop-outs (Jan-Jun / Jul-Oct / 2021-25); the median stopped trade was only +0.21R our way at best and was out in 33 min (Jan-Jun).

A careful-human skip list (against both trends / late / news within 30 min / prior-day level under 1R ahead) flags 45% of the losing $ but also 19% of the winning $ (Jan-Jun): skipping them = -$4,320 Jan-Jun, -$5,518 Jul-Oct, +$3,264 in 2021-25.

Why winners win (Jan-Jun): the best 20% of winners made +$33,838 (100% of the net); the median winner went only 0.19R against us first and took 106 min; 62% of winners came on days that closed our way (losers 31%).

Hindsight, not a rule: on days that closed our way the trades made +$27,744 / +$9,375 / +$52,621, on days that closed against us +$6,517 / +$544 / -$50,950 (Jan-Jun / Jul-Oct / 2021-25). The day's direction is only known after the close.

Known at the entry, nothing separates losers from winners better than chance: 18 of 86 fact buckets were worse (or better) in all three periods, vs 15.4 on average with the results shuffled (p 0.274).

say: Jan-Jun 2026: 98 losing trades cost -$8,815: never worked 71%, worked then turned 19%, shaken out then went our way 11%, news 0%.
Jul-Oct 2026: 49 losing trades cost -$4,351: never worked 75%, worked then turned 17%, shaken out then went our way 4%, news 4%.
2021-25: 929 losing trades cost -$81,497: never worked 67%, worked then turned 16%, shaken out then went our way 16%, news 1%.

Some stops are shake-outs (wider stops were tested before and lost: the other stop-outs get bigger): a stop 50% wider would have reached +1R first on 31.0% / 29.4% / 29.9% of stop-outs (Jan-Jun / Jul-Oct / 2021-25); the median stopped trade was only +0.19R our way at best and was out in 12 min (Jan-Jun).

A careful-human skip list (against both trends / late / news within 30 min / prior-day level under 1R ahead) flags 64% of the losing $ but also 63% of the winning $ (Jan-Jun): skipping them = -$3,419 Jan-Jun, -$2,242 Jul-Oct, -$2,676 in 2021-25.

Why winners win (Jan-Jun): the best 20% of winners made +$7,332 (133% of the net); the median winner went only 0.27R against us first and took 31 min; 98% of winners came on days that closed our way (losers 87%).

Hindsight, not a rule: on days that closed our way the trades made +$6,623 / +$3,009 / +$12,398, on days that closed against us -$1,110 / -$865 / -$7,828 (Jan-Jun / Jul-Oct / 2021-25). The day's direction is only known after the close.
Known at the entry, nothing separates losers from winners better than chance: 7 of 66 fact buckets were worse (or better) in all three periods, vs 14.2 on average with the results shuffled (p 0.97).
465 bets 2026-08-03 to 2026-11-18: 70% won, +$2,234 at $15 a bet. A loss costs $15.27, a win pays $13.36: K8 wins by being right often, not big.
Why it wins: the cheap fills. Bets bought under 50c made +$1,106 of the +$2,234 (64% won, $18.25 a win); at 60c+ they win 83% but pay $7.87, +$307 in total. A price creeping up is the real threat.
Why it loses: gold and silver of the same window move together. Of 232 windows both won 139 and both lost 45 times: the 6 legs are closer to 3 bets a day, so a bad day costs 2 x $15.
Held-out weeks (test): 68% won, +$945; 2 of 16 weeks lost money, the newest week -$74.
